checked_sources.supports: 176-day solar day vs ~88-day year and ~59-day rotation
runaway greenhouse; rotation 243 days, year 225 days, solar day 117 days
hydrogen/helium composition; Great Red Spot; no true surface and deep pressure
Olympus Mons is the Solar System’s largest volcano
only planet with average density below water; no true surface; pressure at depth
97.77-degree axial tilt causes extreme seasons; Uranus second least dense
Triton retrograde relative to Neptune’s rotation
Triton’s retrograde orbit and unusual orbital inclination
Triton orbital plane inclined 156.8 degrees to Neptune’s equator; motion retrograde

decisions.note: NASA Venus facts directly attributes Venus’s extreme surface heat to its dense runaway-greenhouse atmosphere. Options are parallel in length and only this answer fits; difficulty 3 seems plausible.

NASA Mercury facts distinguishes 176-day solar day from 88-day year and 59-day axial rotation, making the noon-to-noon answer unique. Options have no obvious length giveaway; difficulty 6 is plausible because it distinguishes three periods.
NASA Jupiter facts says it is mostly hydrogen and helium and supports the deeper hydrogen explanation. Wrong pairs are distinct; difficulty 3 seems plausible.

NASA Mars facts explicitly calls Olympus Mons the Solar System’s largest volcano, so Mars is uniquely correct. The key explanation mentions an impact crater and Earth’s highest mountain although neither is in the choices; replace with a short explanation mapping directly to the four planet options. Difficulty 3 reasonable.

NASA Saturn facts says Saturn is the only planet with average density below water. The explanation correctly limits this to average whole-planet density. Difficulty 5 may be high for a common fact, but this is subjective.
NASA Uranus facts gives 97.77° tilt and calls it the cause of the Solar System’s most extreme seasons, including 21-year dark winters. Distractors do not fit that mechanism; difficulty 5 plausible.

NASA Neptune facts and its Triton page support retrograde motion. The key also asserts Triton is neither polar nor in the ring plane, but its source list only cites Neptune facts. Add the Triton page and an orientation reference such as NASA NTRS’s paper giving inclination 156.8° relative to Neptune’s equator, or trim those distractor rationales. The polar-orbit option may confuse because orbital plane and direction are separate properties. Difficulty 4 plausible.
NASA Jupiter facts identifies the Great Red Spot as an atmospheric storm and says Jupiter has no true surface. Its three alternatives are surface-geology interpretations. Difficulty 2 plausible.
NASA Venus facts gives 243-day axial rotation, 225-day year, and 117-day solar day. The first option is uniquely correct; options compare periods in parallel. Difficulty 6 plausible.

NASA Saturn facts supports no true surface and increasing deep pressure/temperature; NASA Jupiter facts supports the same for Jupiter. Since the stem names both and the explanation covers both, add Jupiter to this record’s sources (it is already in the source ledger), or narrow the stem to Saturn. Intended answer is unique; difficulty 4 plausible.
